title: 16S rRNA Library Preparation Protocol
author: Kara Tinker
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jz4cp8w
materials: Verify PCR product by gel electrophoresis.
Verify subpool products by gel electrophoresis.

steps.title: Dilute DNA samples
steps.instruction: Dilute each DNA sample to a concentration of approximately 2–5 ng/µL; if a sample is already below 2 ng/µL, use it without dilution.

steps.title: Set up first PCR reactions
steps.instruction: Prepare duplicate 10 µL PCR reactions (base sample and technical replicate) by mixing for each reaction: 4.7 µL H₂O, 2.0 µL 5X Q5 Hot Start Buffer, 0.5 µL 10 µM forward primer (505F), 0.5 µL 10 µM reverse primer (806R), 0.2 µL 10 mM dNTPs, and 0.1 µL Q5 Hot Start DNA Polymerase. Keep dNTPs on ice and polymerase on ice; buffer and primers may be at room temperature. Prepare mix for the number of reactions plus one extra to avoid shortage. Distribute 8 µL of this mix into each PCR tube and add 2 µL of the diluted DNA (total volume 10 µL).

steps.title: Run first PCR
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in a thermocycler and run the first PCR program as specified in the protocol (program details not provided in the source text).

steps.title: Prepare second PCR mix
steps.instruction: While the first PCR is cycling, prepare a second‑round 30 µL reaction mix for each tube (including one extra). For each reaction combine: 11.1 µL H₂O, 6.0 µL 5X Q5 Hot Start Buffer, 1.5 µL 10 µM 806_BCR primer, 0.6 µL 10 mM dNTPs, and 0.3 µL Q5 Hot Start DNA Polymerase. After the first PCR finishes, keep the tubes on a cold block, dispense 21 µL of the second‑mix into each new tube, add 9 µL of the corresponding first‑PCR product, and mix by pipetting up and down.

steps.title: Run second PCR
steps.instruction: Run the second‑round PCR on a thermocycler using the program described in the protocol (program details not provided in the source text).

steps.title: Purify PCR products
steps.instruction: Purify the completed PCR reactions with the Omega Bio‑Tek E.Z.N.A. Cycle‑Pure Kit following the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Quantify and store amplicons
steps.instruction: Measure each purified amplicon’s concentration and A260/A280 ratio using a NanoDrop spectrophotometer, record the values, and store the samples at –20 °C.

steps.title: Create subpools of amplicons
steps.instruction: For each subpool, combine an equal amount of amplicon from each sample (generally 50 ng per sample, adjusting as necessary) to form subpools containing 15–30 distinct samples.

steps.title: Pool subpools for sequencing
steps.instruction: Combine equal amounts of amplicon from each subpool to generate the final pooled library, then submit the library for sequencing.
